correctness.rationale: Centering the two symmetric bodies makes both support functions even. For each fixed orthogonal map, residual translation contributes an odd linear function. Antipodal pairing and strict convexity of |x|^p show that zero residual translation uniquely minimizes the p-th power of the distance. A nonzero linear functional is nonzero off a great subsphere of measure zero, making the integrated comparison strict. Hence every global optimal isometry must align centers. The bundled checker replays the scalar strict-convexity inequality and an independent antipodal numerical regression.

value.rationale: All centrally symmetric convex bodies form a fundamental isometry-invariant class in every dimension. The theorem completely solves the translation component of Lp matching on that class for every orientation and gives a canonical positive subclass answer to a published p>2 selector problem. It separates translation from rotation by a structural parity mechanism, rather than by finite computation or a narrow parameter choice.
